status: This iteration is verified; the ongoing game interaction objective is not complete.

changes.result: Flying cards, attacks, confirmed impact, health trails and combat text follow the existing playback speed. Normal scale 1, fast scale 2/7, relaxed scale capped at 2. Accepted commands and current decisions remain immediate.
changes.problem: Fast autoplay advanced every 100 ms while battle effects retained standard duration, accumulating earlier visual results.

changes.result: Rebase active cue start times using their previous normalized age. Preserve current position, text layout, health remainder and face handoff while changing remaining duration.
changes.problem: Switching playback speed could restart an in-progress animation if its time base changed directly.

changes.result: The existing LayoutUpdated handler requests a render only when public face handoff changes. No second subscription or new persistent layout cache.
changes.problem: A public card container could complete layout after the layer drew its fallback face; the static face then appeared while the old drawing remained cached.

implementation.uses: Existing committed public cues, visible hand origins, public card anchors and playback selection.

routine.scope: Measured routine from tools/VerificationScopes.psd1; not manual full verification or single-action UI latency.

checks: Real native Slash card 9 commits exactly once; at 120 ms in fast mode no flying face remains and the public face is visible. Effects expire without altering all eight player snapshots.
Real native Dodge card 45 commits 14 -> 15 once. Normal -> relaxed -> fast keeps moving image bounds within 0.01 DIP on each speed switch; arrival occurs once and four player views remain unchanged.
Manual save/load retains selected fast speed and restores the binding without replaying historical cues.
Public HP remainder geometry stays within 0.01 DIP across fast -> relaxed; remaining trail retreats and expires, and motion toggles do not replay history.

Attack approach, confirmed impact, HP and damage text match normal rendering at corresponding visual ages 0.182, 0.651 and 1.197 seconds with fast times compressed by 2/7; unchanged pixel tolerance is 2 channels.

Injected frame clock rounds elapsed seconds to timestamp resolution. The diagnostic mismatch at phase 3 came from TimeSpan double conversion truncation by one tick; no product behavior or assertion tolerance was weakened.
Existing public privacy, distinct effects, skill text, hand origin, single-face handoff, physical suit/rank, rescue completion, playback, sound routing and table controls passed.

motion.description: Fresh native WPF tables, one accepted physical Slash per recording, injected wall clock, 30 frames at 40 ms. Fast animation finishes early and the remaining frames hold the final state.

limitations: Offscreen native WPF control/render checks and injected clocks do not establish physical foreground mouse/keyboard, multi-DPI or audible speaker acceptance.
The sound routing regression passed; actual audio device output was not exercised.
No manual full verification, release, packaging, commit or push.
The wider battle presentation goal remains active; chained effects and multi-target result staging still need further iteration.
